prompt:
The diagram below shows how wool is produced on a farm and turned into yarn at a mill.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
instruction_line: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

visual.alt: An eight-stage linear process diagram showing wool starting with shearing on the farm, then being washed, dried, combed, spun and dyed, and shipped out on reels at the mill; the short fibres separated during combing go to felt-making.

key_points: The process is linear and has eight stages: it starts with the live animal and ends with yarn ready to be sent out, with no cycle back to the start
The diagram is split into two sections: the first two stages (shearing and the hand-sorting and rolling of the fleece) take place on the farm, and the remaining six stages take place at the mill
Cleaning happens in two steps: the wool is first washed in warm water to remove the grease, then dried in warm air
There is a single side branch at the combing stage: the short fibres are separated out and sent to felt-making, and only the long fibres continue on to become yarn
Becoming yarn involves two processes — the fibres being drawn out and twisted, then dyed in large vats
Shearing taking place once a year, in spring, is the only piece of time information in the diagram
common_mistakes: Not using the passive voice (are shorn, is washed, are combed) and inventing a subject for every sentence ('the farmer cuts the wool')
Leaving out the side branch where the short fibres are separated
Not marking the transition between the farm and the mill
Adding information not in the diagram (how many kilos of wool, how many hours the process takes, what it costs)
Not using stage connectors ('first', 'once the wool has been dried', 'at the final stage') and stringing eight sentences one after another
topic: wool production and how it is turned into yarn
